language_wrapper: Consider a cyclic necklace with {start_n} through {end_n} beads: for each integer n in this range, take an n-gon whose vertices ("beads") are initially labeled 0. A move consists of choosing two adjacent beads and increasing both their labels by 1. If it is possible, after more than 0 moves, to make all n bead labels equal, define g(n) to be the minimal number of moves needed; otherwise set g(n) = 0. Compute the sum S = sum_{n={start_n}}^{n={end_n}} g(n).
hardness_rationale: This family elevates the core idea of equalizing aggregate quantities via pairwise-adjacent increments to a global, parity-sensitive cyclic constraint. The key structural transition is from a 2D grid to a cycle where feasibility and optimality are governed by graph factor theory (existence of perfect matchings versus 2-factors on cycles) and parity/degree-sum arguments. Proving minimality requires leveraging that: (i) a single move contributes degree 1 to exactly two adjacent vertices; (ii) when n is even, a perfect matching achieves uniform degree 1 across all vertices (hence minimal n/2 moves), while when n is odd no perfect matching exists, forcing degree at least 2 at each vertex and exactly n moves via the unique 2-regular factor on C_n. Summing these exact minima over an interval requires careful parity partitioning, and the underlying proof draws on graph factorization rather than the local row/column-sum strategies of the seed, thus changing and deepening the approach.
notes: Proof of correctness: Let C_n be the cycle graph on n vertices; a move increases by 1 the labels on the endpoints of a chosen edge, so the label vector is the vertex-degree vector of a nonnegative integer edge-multiset X on C_n. The total of all labels equals 2|X|, twice the number of moves. To make all labels equal to some k>0, we require a k-regular spanning multigraph on C_n, i.e., sum of incident multiplicities at each vertex equals k. Minimal |X| occurs for the smallest feasible k. For even n, C_n has a perfect matching, i.e., a 1-regular spanning subgraph, so k=1 is feasible and |X|=n/2 is achievable. For odd n, no perfect matching exists on C_n, hence k cannot be 1; the next possibility is k=2, and the unique 2-regular simple factor is the cycle itself (take each edge once), yielding |X|=n moves, which is minimal since any k>=2 implies |X|=kn/2 >= n. Therefore g(n)=n/2 for even n and g(n)=n for odd n. The verifier computes S by summing these exact values over the given interval. This family preserves the pairwise-adjacency increment core but demands graph factorization and parity arguments rather than the row/column lattice flow techniques used for grids.
source_question: In an \(n\times n\) (\(n\in\mathbb{N}^*, n\geq2\)) chessboard, each unit square is filled with the number \(0\). In each operation, two unit squares with a common side are selected, and the numbers in them are both increased by \(1\). If it is possible, through several (more than \(0\) times) operations, to make the sum of the numbers in each row and each column be the same value, then the minimum number of operations is denoted as \(f(n)\); if there is no such operation, then \(f(n) = 0\). Find \(\sum_{i = 2}^{2025}f(i)\).
